transcript_text:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-20
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (AstraNova - Head of ML), Daniel Park (AstraNova - Platform), Omar El-Sayed (AstraNova - Product)

Summary:
Quick scoping for a 6-week POC (they call it Flightpath) to validate model quality for logistics routing notes + customer message triage across EN/ES/FR. Main constraints: sub-200ms 95th tail for short queries desired, accuracy on intent extraction >92% on labeled set, and strict data residency (EU region for some workloads). They want a shortlist of open models and a concrete bench plan + timeline.

Topics:
- Success criteria (latency, accuracy, throughput, cost)
- Workload sizing and expected QPS
- Benchmark plan and metrics
- Model shortlist: tradeoffs for multilingual + domain adaptation
- Deployment modes: hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Lena from Redwood, AE on the account, with Marcus our SE. How are you all?
[00:06] Priya: Hi Lena, hi Marcus. Good, thanks. We've been looking forward to nailing down the POC scope.
[00:12] Marcus: Great. High level, we'd like to understand your exact success criteria, your traffic patterns, and what "good" looks like for QA on routing notes and triage.
[00:20] Daniel: Right. For context, we get about 650k messages a day across channels, but the POC only needs to cover a 10k/day slice we can isolate. Peak QPS for that slice is around 10 requests/sec, typical payload 120-350 tokens.
[00:34] Omar: And multilingual — English is 70%, Spanish 20%, French 10%. We need the models to handle terse messages and also longer driver notes (~800 tokens) for summarization.
[00:46] Priya: Success criteria: intent/extraction F1 >0.92 on our labeled set, summarization ROUGE-L that matches baseline within 5 points, latency SLO 95th <200ms for short queries, and cost per 1k tokens under our pilot budget, obviously. Also SOC2 is a must and EU data residency for EU customer data.
[01:05] Marcus: Good. A couple clarifying q's — when you say 200ms, is that observed from your edge to model return, or just model inference time?
[01:12] Daniel: Model inference time. Edge-to-edge adds another ~20-40ms.
[01:18] Lena: For the POC, we typically run both hosted and dedicated mocks to show the delta. For small-scale benching, hosted is fastest to iterate; Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale. Private VPC is possible but adds ops time.
[01:32] Priya: Ops overhead is a concern — our infra team prefers VPC because of logging and KMS controls. But for speed to result, hosted is appealing.
[01:40] Marcus: Understood. On models, our recommendation is to test a spectrum: a compact low-latency model, a mid-size best-cost model, and a larger quality-focused one. For multilingual and domain robustness, we usually include a multilingual-tuned open model and a generic LLM baseline.
[01:54] Priya: Can you name the open models?
[01:57] Marcus: Sure — rough names on our shortlist: Marathon-13B-ML (multilingual-tuned), AtlasLite-7B (fast low-latency), and Peregrine-70B (higher quality, longer context). We'll also include a quantized 13B variant to test 8-bit perf/cost tradeoffs.
[02:14] Omar: Are those all open weights? Licensing is important for us.
[02:17] Lena: Yes, all are permissive for commercial use — we'll include license notes. Also we'll include a vendor-managed competitor run if you want a like-for-like comparison (you mentioned CloudEndpointAI in your RFP).
[02:26] Speaker 4: (muffled) — also curious about hallucination controls.
[02:29] Marcus: For hallucination, POC will include prompt evals and safety/regression tests. We'll track hallucination rate per 1k tokens on labeled truth set.
[02:37] Priya: Great. For benchmarks — what metrics will you provide out-of-the-box?
[02:41] Marcus: We'll run latency (p50/p95), tokens/sec, cost per token at current running config, accuracy metrics for your intent/extraction, ROUGE for summarization, multilingual accuracy by language slice, and a hallucination score. We'll also produce per-route traces and per-token cost breakdown so you can decide on batching/kv cache rules.
[03:00] Daniel: About KV cache — we do caching of conversation context, will Redwood's runtime let us reuse the KV to reduce tokens?
[03:06] Marcus: Yes, we have automatic KV/prefix caching and continuous batching which drastically reduces unit cost for repeated context. We'll show two bench scenarios: cold start and warm with KV cache. Note: in transcription sometimes "KV" becomes "kay vee" in logs, so just flagging that.
[03:20] Priya: Timelines? If we start next week, how long to get meaningful bench numbers?
[03:24] Lena: If you can provide the samples by Monday (2026-11-21), Marcus can spin up the harness and run initial microbenches in 48–72 hours. Full evaluation across 3 models and multilingual splits takes ~4 business days once harnessed. So deliverables by 2026-11-25 with a results review the week of 2026-11-29.
[03:45] Omar: Any special infra needs? We want to run the POC in EU region and also test a Dedicated pool.
[03:51] Marcus: We'll provision region-matched instances. Dedicated pool can be emulated for cost profiling, but true Dedicated requires a short provisioning lead (~5 business days) if you want reserved capacity. For the pilot we recommend hosted with Dedicated cost projection.
[04:05] Priya: Security — what about KMS integration and audit logs?
[04:09] Lena: We integrate with customer KMS for Private deployments. Hosted supports encrypted-at-rest and we can enable audit log retention for the pilot. We'll attach SOC2 report and our security whitepaper in the follow-up.
[04:19] Daniel: How do we interpret the cost numbers? We have a target pilot budget and need a clear band for cost per 1k tokens depending on model and quantization.
[04:27] Marcus: Our bench output will include cost per 1k tokens for each model/config, and an estimated monthly projection for your expected QPS. We'll include cost sensitivity to batching and 8-bit quantization.
[04:36] Priya: For multilingual, do you recommend translating to English and run a single model, or use a multilingual model?
[04:41] Marcus: For terse messages, translation to English can be reasonable but adds latency and error. For high accuracy in Spanish/French, the multilingual-tuned Marathon-13B-ML showed fewer drop-offs in our internal evals — we'll test both translation pipeline vs native multilingual model as part of the POC.
[04:58] Omar: What about long driver notes (~800 tokens)? Peregrine-70B handles longer context but it's heavier; can we do summarization on a mid-size model with chunking?
[05:06] Marcus: Yes, chunk-and-merge summarization is a common pattern. We'll bench chunking overhead vs single-pass on long context. Expect p95 for long summarization to be higher than short queries; we'll capture that in the report.
[05:18] Priya: Any special evaluation artifacts you need from us?
[05:21] Marcus: Labeled intent/extraction set, summarization references for ~1k examples, and a 1k sample of multilingual short messages. Ideally in CSV/JSON Lines, with schema: id, lang, text, label(s).
[05:34] Priya: We'll produce that — Daniel will coordinate upload.
[05:37] Daniel: Yep, I'll upload to the S3 share, link to be provided.
[05:40] Lena: Next steps recap — we'll send benchmark template and S3 instructions, Marcus will run initial microbench and deliver results by 11/25, Lena will send SOW and pricing bands.
[05:50] Priya: Sounds good. A couple of concerns from procurement — licensing, auditability, and rollback if models regress.
[05:56] Lena: We'll include license summaries and an eval rollback plan. Also propose a canary rollout pattern for pilot to reduce risk.
[06:04] Omar: Competitors — we did talk to Weights&Measures, they push an ensemble approach; curious to see Redwood's per-token cost vs an ensemble.
[06:12] Marcus: We'll include a competitor comparison table for throughput/cost where publicly available.
[06:16] Lena: Any other questions?
[06:18] Speaker 4: None here.
[06:20] Lena: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with artifacts.

Closing notes:
- Proposed POC: 6 weeks with core benching and one-week integration after model selection.
- Deliverables: benchmark report (latency/cost/accuracy/hallucination), recommended model + quantization config, SOW and pricing bands, deployment notes for hosted + dedicated projection, security docs.

References mentioned during call:
- Benchmark template (link placeholder)

End of transcript.
